source_span: those buffers are now seen as fading, leaving oil prices increasingly vulnerable to further geopolitical disruptions... we are hard-pressed to see a resolution to energy price pressures anytime soon and incorporate features of a higher oil risk-premium into the baseline
source_chain: Supply-chain disruptions (Mideast export routes, pipeline outages, shipping bottlenecks, tanker/refinery constraints, low European fuel stocks) have exhausted the buffers that absorbed the earlier shock, therefore oil prices are durably elevated and vulnerable to further disruption (not a temporary premium), therefore core PCE is revised up and the Fed adds two more 25bp hikes (Dec/March) to 4.25-4.50%; invalidated only by an actual resolution of the Mideast conflict, which MS says it no longer expects.
pulse_chain: Brent's $16 premium over JPMorgan's $90 fair value prices in feared supply losses (4mb/d) that haven't materialized, therefore a diplomacy headline can erase the crude premium instantly, therefore refined-fuel scarcity (BofA: record diesel, refineries at 97% capacity) is separable and structural and keeps inflation sticky and the hikes intact; invalidated by Thursday's Trump-Xi meeting, JPMorgan's named catalyst.
why: None of the theme's load-bearing figures or bank attributions ($90 JPMorgan fair value, $16 premium, 4mb/d, 555m/1.6bn barrel draw, $6.31 diesel, BofA's 97% refinery utilization, Goldman's 77th-percentile hedge-fund energy selling, the Trump-Xi invalidation) appear in any 2026-09-21 source file, and the one note that actually argues an oil risk premium (Morgan Stanley) argues the opposite mechanism -- that faded buffers make the price rise durable rather than a headline-reversible political premium -- with a different invalidation (Mideast de-escalation, not a Trump-Xi meeting).
